characters.name: Elkanah
characters.note: Hannah's husband, father of Samuel; also 'the man Elkanah' (1:21, 2:11, 2:20 blessing context). Also Elkanah of 1:1 is the same person; the Elkanah in the genealogy of 1:1 (son of Jeroham) is an ancestor, not on stage — treated as mentioned only within the same entry's genealogy, not a separate character needed for illustration. The Elkanah blessed in 2:20 is the same husband of Hannah. (The Elkanah in 1 Chronicles 6 is a different person and does not appear here.)

characters.name: Hannah
characters.note: Wife of Elkanah, mother of Samuel; prays silently, later sings the hymn of 2:1-10.

characters.name: Peninnah
characters.note: Elkanah's other wife, mother of his children; taunts Hannah.

characters.name: Samuel
characters.note: Son of Elkanah and Hannah; dedicated at Shiloh, called by Yahweh as a child, later prophet and judge who anoints Saul.

characters.name: Eli
characters.note: High priest at Shiloh, nearly blind, heavy; judges Israel forty years; dies falling from his seat.

characters.name: Hophni
characters.note: Eli's son, corrupt priest; dies when the ark is captured.

characters.name: Phinehas
characters.note: Eli's son, corrupt priest; dies with the ark; husband of Phinehas' wife.

characters.name: Phinehas' wife
characters.note: Unnamed daughter-in-law of Eli; dies giving birth to Ichabod.

characters.name: Ichabod
characters.note: Newborn son of Phinehas; named 'the glory has departed'.

characters.name: The man of God
characters.note: Unnamed prophet who denounces Eli's house (2:27-36).

characters.name: The man of Benjamin
characters.note: Unnamed survivor who runs from the battle to Shiloh with news (4:12-17).

characters.name: The Philistines
characters.note: Israel's enemy; acts as army and as five lords ruling Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, Ekron.

characters.name: Israel / the men of Israel
characters.note: Israel's army and people as a group.

characters.name: The men of Beth Shemesh
characters.note: Reapers who receive the ark; some struck for looking into it.

characters.name: The men of Jabesh Gilead
characters.note: Besieged by Nahash; later rescue Saul's body.

characters.name: Kish
characters.note: Benjamite father of Saul; loses his donkeys.

characters.name: Saul
characters.note: Son of Kish, anointed first king of Israel; tall; hunts David; dies on Gilboa.

characters.name: Saul's servant
characters.note: Unnamed attendant who accompanies Saul seeking donkeys.

characters.name: Saul's uncle
characters.note: Unnamed; questions Saul about his trip (10:14-16).

characters.name: Jonathan
characters.note: Saul's son, David's beloved friend; strikes the Philistine garrison; makes covenants with David; dies on Gilboa.

characters.name: Nahash
aliases: the king of the children of Ammon
characters.note: Ammonite king who besieges Jabesh Gilead.

characters.name: Abner
characters.note: Saul's army commander; sleeps at Saul's side in camp.

characters.name: Doeg
characters.note: Saul's Edomite herdsman; informs on Ahimelech and slaughters the priests of Nob.

characters.name: Ahimelech
characters.note: Priest at Nob who helps David; executed with his house.

characters.name: Abiathar
characters.note: Son of Ahimelech who escapes the Nob massacre and joins David with the ephod.

characters.name: Achish
characters.note: Philistine king of Gath who shelters David and gives him Ziklag.

characters.name: Gad
characters.note: Prophet who tells David to leave the stronghold for Judah (22:5).

characters.name: Nabal
characters.note: Rich, surly shepherd of Maon/Carmel; refuses David; struck dead by Yahweh.

characters.name: Abigail
characters.note: Intelligent, beautiful wife of Nabal; appeases David with provisions; becomes David's wife.

characters.name: Ahinoam
characters.note: David's wife from Jezreel; captured by Amalekites and rescued.

characters.name: Michal
characters.note: Saul's daughter given to David; Saul later gives her to Palti (mentioned only in this part).

characters.name: Palti
characters.note: Man of Gallim to whom Saul gives Michal (25:44, mentioned only).

characters.name: Abishai
characters.note: David's nephew who volunteers to strike Saul in the camp (26:6-11).

characters.name: Ahimelech the Hittite
characters.note: Hittite among David's men invited to the night raid (26:6).

characters.name: Joab
characters.note: Brother of Abishai, named only (26:6, mentioned only).

characters.name: The woman who has a familiar spirit
characters.note: Medium at Endor whom Saul visits in disguise; she conjures Samuel.

characters.name: The Egyptian
characters.note: Sick servant found in the field who guides David to the Amalekite camp (30:11-15).

characters.name: Saul's armor bearer
characters.note: Refuses to kill Saul, then falls on his own sword (31:4-5).

characters.name: Abinadab of Kiriath Jearim
characters.note: Man in whose house the ark is kept; father of Eleazar (7:1).

characters.name: Eleazar
characters.note: Son of Abinadab, consecrated to keep the ark (7:1).

characters.name: Abinadab son of Saul
characters.note: Saul's son killed on Gilboa (31:2); distinct from Abinadab of Kiriath Jearim.

characters.name: Malchishua
characters.note: Saul's son killed on Gilboa (31:2).

characters.name: Goliath
characters.note: The giant slain by David in the valley of Elah; his sword is kept at Nob (21:9, mentioned only).

characters.name: Jesse
characters.note: David's father; named in taunts and references (mentioned only in this part).

characters.name: Moses
characters.note: Named in Samuel's farewell speech (12:6, 12:8, mentioned only).

characters.name: Aaron
characters.note: Named in Samuel's farewell speech (12:6, 12:8, mentioned only).

characters.name: Jacob
characters.note: Named in Samuel's speech (12:8, mentioned only).

characters.name: Sisera
aliases: captain of the army of Hazor
characters.note: Named in Samuel's speech (12:9, mentioned only).

characters.name: Jephthah
characters.note: Former deliverers named in Samuel's speech (12:11, mentioned only).

characters.name: Rachel
characters.note: Her tomb is a landmark in Saul's anointing signs (10:2, mentioned only).

characters.name: David
characters.note: Jesse's son, anointed successor to Saul; fugitive, then leader of 600 men; spares Saul twice; becomes husband of Abigail and Ahinoam.

characters.name: David's men
characters.note: The band of distressed men who gather to David and act as a group.

characters.name: The Amalekites
characters.note: Raiders who burn Ziklag and carry off the women; defeated by David (30:1-20).

characters.name: Saul's servants / the guard
characters.note: Courtiers around Saul; refuse to kill the priests (22:6-17, 28:7-8).

characters.name: The Ziphites
characters.note: Men of Ziph who betray David's hiding place to Saul twice (23:19, 26:1).

characters.name: The band of prophets
characters.note: Ecstatic procession with lute, tambourine, pipe and harp met by Saul (10:5-13).

characters.name: The elders of Judah
characters.note: Receive David's plunder gifts (30:26-31).

locations.name: Ramah
locations.note: Elkanah's and Samuel's home town in the hill country of Ephraim.

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.note: Sanctuary where Eli serves and the ark rests; Samuel ministers here.

locations.name: Ebenezer
locations.note: Battle camp site (ch 4) and the memorial stone Samuel names (7:12).

locations.name: Aphek
locations.note: Philistine battle camp (ch 4) and muster point (29:1).

locations.name: Ashdod
locations.note: Philistine city where the ark topples the idol Dagon.

locations.name: Gath
locations.note: Philistine city; Achish's capital; David flees here twice.

locations.name: Ekron
locations.note: Philistine city struck by plague; the lords return here.

locations.name: Beth Shemesh
locations.note: Israelite town where the cart with the ark arrives during wheat harvest.

locations.name: Kiriath Jearim
locations.note: Town where the ark is kept twenty years in Abinadab's house.

locations.name: Mizpah
locations.note: Gathering place for prayer, battle and Saul's election.

locations.name: Gilgal
locations.note: Saul is made king here; Samuel's farewell address.

locations.name: Beersheba
locations.note: Southern town where Samuel's sons judge; southern boundary marker.

locations.name: Bethel
locations.note: Circuit town of Samuel's judging; destination of the three men in Saul's signs.

locations.name: Gibeah
locations.note: Saul's hometown and capital; his spear-cast at Jonathan; the field nearby.

locations.name: Jabesh Gilead
locations.note: Transjordan town besieged by Nahash; later buries Saul's body under the tamarisk.

locations.name: Bezek
locations.note: Muster point where Saul counts the army (11:8).

locations.name: Geba
locations.note: Philistine outpost Jonathan strikes (13:3).

locations.name: Michmash
locations.note: Where Saul stations two thousand men (13:2).

locations.name: Nob
locations.note: Priestly town where Ahimelech gives David bread and Goliath's sword.

locations.name: The cave of Adullam
locations.note: David's refuge where his band gathers.

locations.name: Mizpeh of Moab
locations.note: Where David shelters his parents with the king of Moab.

locations.name: The forest of Hereth
locations.note: Forest in Judah where David goes at Gad's word.

locations.name: Keilah
locations.note: Walled town David saves from the Philistines, then leaves.

locations.name: The wilderness of Ziph
locations.note: Desert refuge where Saul hunts David twice.

locations.name: The wilderness of Maon
locations.note: Desert where Saul nearly traps David; Nabal's home region.

locations.name: En Gedi
aliases: the rocks of the wild goats
locations.note: Oasis wilderness where David spares Saul in a cave.

locations.name: Carmel
locations.note: Judah town where Nabal shears sheep and Abigail meets David.

locations.name: The wilderness of Paran
locations.note: Desert David enters after Samuel's death (25:1).

locations.name: Ziklag
locations.note: Philistine town Achish gives David; burned by Amalekites.

locations.name: The brook Besor
locations.note: Stream where two hundred of David's men stay behind (30:9-21).

locations.name: Endor
locations.note: Village of the medium Saul visits by night.

locations.name: Shunem
locations.note: Philistine camp before the final battle (28:4).

locations.name: Mount Gilboa
locations.note: Mountain where Israel camps and Saul and his sons die.

locations.name: Beth Shan
locations.note: Philistine town where Saul's body is fastened to the wall.

locations.name: The field
locations.note: Open field near Gibeah where Jonathan and David meet and the arrow sign is given.

locations.name: The valley of Elah
locations.note: Where David killed Goliath (21:9, mentioned only).

locations.name: Jezreel
locations.note: Israelite camp by the spring before the final battle (29:1).

locations.name: Hebron
locations.note: Judah town receiving David's plunder gift (30:31).

brief.era: Iron Age Israel, roughly 1050-1010 BC: village life, tribal militias, chariot-less armies with slings, spears, swords and bows.
brief.place: Hill country of Ephraim and Judah, Philistine coastal plain (Ashdod, Gath, Ekron), desert strongholds of Ziph, Maon and En Gedi, Mount Gilboa.
brief.dress: Men in knee-length wool tunics with cloaks and sashes; priests in linen ephods (Samuel as a boy wears a little linen ephod and a yearly robe from Hannah); Saul and David armed with spear and sword; women in long robes with head coverings; Saul disguises himself in commoner's clothes for Endor.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Shiloh's tent-tabernacle with doorposts, altar and the lamp of God; the ark of the covenant with cherubim (a gold-covered chest, never an open idol); Dagon's fallen idol in Ashdod; a new cart drawn by two milk cows with golden tumor and mouse images; Samuel's memorial stone; Saul's spear stuck in the ground by his head; Goliath's great sword wrapped in cloth behind the ephod at Nob; Abigail's donkeys loaded with bread, wine, sheep, raisins and fig cakes; the witch's house with a fattened calf and unleavened bread.
depiction_rules: Yahweh is never shown as a figure; his presence may be suggested by light, a voice, or the ark.
The ark of the covenant is a chest with winged cherubim on its lid, carried by poles or on a cart.
Samuel's ghost at Endor rises as an old man covered with a robe, perceived as 'a god coming up out of the earth' - show him emerging from the ground, luminous, not a living man.
Dagon is a fisherman-idol; show him toppled, head and hands broken off on the threshold.
Hannah prays with only her lips moving, mistaken for drunkenness.
Saul is consistently taller than everyone 'from the shoulders upward'.
